  who cannot stay, who never says goodbye,
  only moves on, still singing.

✻ Churned for 14s · done 4:46 AM

❯ Write a 100-word poem about fire, no tools.

● Fire begins as a small persuasion,
  a match's brief argument with the dark.
  It climbs the kindling like a rumor,
  teaching dry wood its final language.
  We gather close, palms open,
  faces painted in restless gold.
  It tells the oldest stories:
  of caves and wolves kept at the edge,
  of bread, of iron, of long winters survived.
  It is hunger with a beautiful face,
  eating the forest, the letter, the year,
  giving back only warmth and ash.
  I watch the embers breathe and dim,
  small red cities falling asleep,
  and carry their glow to bed,
  a lantern behind my eyes.

✻ Worked for 15s · done 4:47 AM
